findings.source_passage: Still, being among such a large crowd of my fellow humans was a bitter reminder of how normal my boring life was.
findings.why_it_matters: The source's self-deprecating, resigned tone—'bitter reminder,' 'boring life'—is interpretively loaded; the draft softens to 'reminded me how ordinary my life was,' losing the edge of bitterness that establishes Miriam's voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'bitter reminder' phrasing and 'boring life' self-assessment verbatim or very close; these establish her resigned interiority.

findings.source_passage: I glanced out the window and sighed. The world sped by us as a shadow play of colorful lights and figures.
findings.why_it_matters: 'Shadow play of colorful lights and figures' is the only piece of literary, image-driven prose in the chapter—it signals the author's register and frames Miriam's yearning mood. The draft replaces it with 'Lights smeared against the glass,' erasing the distinctive figure.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'the world sped by us as a shadow play of colorful lights and figures' or a near-verbatim version.

findings.source_passage: "This isn't living! This is the preliminaries before death!"
findings.why_it_matters: This comic one-liner is the clearest voice-establishing joke in the chapter—it shows Miriam's dry wit under pressure and is the most quotable line in the source. The draft collapses the whole chase without preserving it.
findings.suggested_fix: Even if the chase is compressed, include Miriam's 'preliminaries before death' line to preserve her comedic voice register.

findings.source_passage: He shook his head. 'It's nothing. Anyway, nice to have met you.' He waved and walked off.
findings.source_locator: Blake exit, after Heather's 'on to you?' line
findings.why_it_matters: Blake's cryptic 'It's nothing' deflection carries interpretive weight as a subtle hint of something sinister; the draft skips his spoken exit and replaces it with a generic 'look that felt like a test,' losing the specific verbal cue.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain Blake's spoken dismissal 'It's nothing' to preserve the subtle menace of his exit.

findings.source_passage: Heather stamped her foot on the ground and slopped puddle water all over herself.
findings.why_it_matters: The comic physical consequence—puddle water soaking Heather after her indignant stamp—is a small but characteristic comic grace note. The draft notes 'ankles splashing through a puddle' but removes the self-drenching payoff.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the detail that her stomp splashed water 'all over herself' for the comic beat.

summary: No high-severity signature losses, but three medium-severity voice flattenings (bitterness framing, 'shadow play' image, and the 'preliminaries before death' joke) collectively thin the chapter's register without crossing the regeneration threshold.
